setup: One stopped native 300 × 19 × 8 hull and one copied fixed-cabin test hull on a new dedicated server. Two survival non-operator player accounts are simulated on the server. The driver called production CabinApproach.begin twice during the same tick. The normal survey interface and its advance terrain loading were outside this test.
limits: First surface-berth planning took 330.3 ms and the second cold berth took 1403.4 ms. Assembly spent 1842.4 ms combined on tick 51. Physics transfer entry took 1008.7 and 2043.9 ms on separate ticks. Ordinary graphical confirmations are scheduled by LandingControl and need a separate concurrent client test.

normalSurvey.setup: Two simulated non-operator survival captains on a loopback-only dedicated Forge server with zero clients. The original wide ship and its copy begin prepositioned near the Moon. Both use normal survey polling and confirm on the same server tick.

fixtureControl.observed: Sending SURVEY once per seat left no live survey by the end of this trial. The retest models the open landing screen polling both surveys while they advance.

normalSurvey.limits: Native assembly still spent 859 and 975 milliseconds on separate ticks. Graphical clients, player discoverability and production server performance were outside this trial.

sharedStoragePreloading.scenario: Two independent loopback dedicated server runs from the same stopped 300×19×8 reference ship. Two simulated survival pilots, normal survey, confirmation and physical passage. No game clients.
sharedStoragePreloading.scope: Both warmers have claimed physical chunk tickets for 54 overlapping ticks. All source and target storage chunks are ready before each portal and the portals use separate ticks. The last dispatch is 27–29 ticks sooner. The second native portal and passage wall time increase in both runs, so these trials do not establish a lower worst-case tick.

hostedFirstGuiAttempt.observed: Both players entered the original Moon and both died during delivery. The first fixture equipped the original pressure suit but not the sealed GalaxySpace suit. The server notice was generic. The rerun uses the same real sealed suit recipes as the existing full-pack lunar test and records original damage sources.

hostedChartReplyRetainsKit.scope: Both Chinese survival clients rendered four sealed suit slots, received the replayed chart opening reply, clicked Back, and landed two prepared 300-block ships on the original Moon. Offline replay independently agreed with the runner. The separate native assembly calls still took 3.66 and 4.39 seconds.

chartReplyInterruptedKit.observed: The captain displayed the sealed equipment page and then resumed the star chart without pressing Back. The engineer pressed Back. A same-ship chart reply can replace the open equipment page. The fix updates the chart behind the equipment page and the regression replays the chart-opening reply while the rendered kit is visible.

nativeBlockOrderComparison.setup: Two paired dedicated Forge servers per arm, two simulated captains each, same 300-block source save and fixture with JDK 17 Flight Recorder enabled. All four halted normally and passed independent save audit.
nativeBlockOrderComparison.decision: Keep the existing move order. The alternate order did not consistently reduce assembly time and both alternate trials had a slower second native portal.

profiledDedicatedAssembly.setup: Parallel survey in a loopback dedicated server with two simulated survival pilots and no client process. JDK 17 Flight Recorder profile settings were enabled.
profiledDedicatedAssembly.observation: Native assembly samples included block storage, height maps, lighting and neighbour notifications, plus chunk access and original block-entity loads. Sampling identifies the active paths but does not assign exact wall-clock time to each one.

hostedArchivedDualLanding.fixture: Two Chinese clients in survival with non-op accounts, two prepared wide ships and original sealed lunar suits.
hostedArchivedDualLanding.workflowFailure: The expected count added the furnace to the hull even though it replaces a side wall block. The corrected replay checks all 20,103 occupied blocks by count, the three actual occupied dimensions, the block entity counts, both player saves, the separate receipts and the exact head and tail cargo slots.

hostedSealedSuitAttempt.limits: The server reported success and a clean shutdown. The fixture supplied both ships and suits. The offline audit failed when the VS storage box was used as the occupied hull size, and the chunk regions were not uploaded by this run.

confirmedSurveyNov23.scope: Two simulated non-op pilots on a dedicated Forge 47.4.28 server with a copy of the previously verified 300-block hull and the normal survey, clear and land server controls. No graphical clients were used.
confirmedSurveyNov23.warnings: The dedicated console reported a Valkyrien Skies chunk-tick timeout during setup and later server tick backlog warnings. Both production handovers, payments and saves still completed. This is a short dual-ship load test.

restorationLogSummaryNov23.scope: Same copied 300 x 19 x 8 hull and mirrored copy as the confirmed survey. No graphical clients. The updated executable changes recovery logging while keeping restoration and post-payment validation.

profile.capture: JFR settings=profile on a separate baseline repeat. Samples show a candidate path but do not isolate a cause of the entire assembly stall.

hostedSummaryRevision.scope: Two hosted Chinese survival clients with cheats off, two prepared original 300-block wide hulls and different lunar sites. The audit reads normal map confirmations, cargo, fees and the closed dedicated-server world.
hostedSummaryRevision.limit: The production assembly calls still occupy separate ticks for approximately 2.72 and 3.06 seconds in the hosted environment. This was a short landing scene with prepared hulls.

hostedProfiledWideBerths.scope: Two hosted Chinese survival clients with cheats disabled confirmed two prepared 300 × 19 × 8 original hulls. Replayed the stopped world independently. The server recorded execution samples at a 5 ms setting while the clients ran on the same isolated runner.

profile.interpretation: The largest cluster is template placement into the VS storage area. Both source cabins were fully loaded. This recording gives a target for finer instrumentation, not an estimate of elapsed time per operation or a before/after speed comparison. There is one Retrofit legacy tile on each tested ship.

hostedWideTemplateTimings.scope: Two ordinary hosted Chinese Forge clients confirmed prepared original hulls. The observer measures inclusive time and call counts within template placement; timings include probe overhead and do not yet separate existing chunk cache hits from misses.

hostedWideChunkReuse.scope: Same two prepared 300-block hulls, Chinese survival clients and instrumented observer on a different hosted runner. Both shut-down worlds passed replay. Timings include instrumentation and variation across runners. Several seconds of assembly stall remain.

hostedWideManagedChunkTasks.scope: Two prepared 300-block original ships with both Chinese survival clients. Measured the inclusive managedBlock time while obtaining chunks during template placement. This includes executing pending server tasks and is not a measurement of idle waiting alone. The same dedicated world passed independent replay.

hostedWidePreloadedFixture.scope: Two fixture-specific VS storage plots were preloaded in advance. Independent audit verified both template destinations had all 40 chunks ready and both survival clients finished landing with the original cargo and fares. Production storage reservation requires separate verification.

hostedWideReservedFailure.failure: After both template placements, the console lookup called Level.getBlockEntity at its estimated coordinates and requested terrain generation. The Overworld aquifer threw an array bounds exception. The engineer died and clean server shutdown failed.

hostedWideConsoleFix.scope: The normal allocator completed two original Moon landings from separate non-operator Chinese survival clients. Independent stopped-world replay verified both hulls, original cargo, fares, occupants and absence of stale VS ships.

hostedWideReservedHandoffFailure.failure: Both assemblies and post-paste console lookups returned. The engineer stayed at the original cabin coordinates, fell from the former cabin elevation and died in the Overworld. Neither ship completed the landing. The server saved normally; no independent stopped-world landing proof was produced.

hostedWideRetainedEmptyPlotFailure.observed: Both relocated consoles were found, but neither empty native reservation became a loaded VS ship. The engineer fell from the old cabin and died. Pinned VS core analysis shows a tick phase deletes ships with mass below 1e-8. Previews now avoid creating a native ship until VS starts assembly.

hostedWidePlotPreview.scope: Two separately rendered Chinese survival clients chose distinct lunar berths. Predictions matched both actual template centers, with 40/40 chunks loaded at each write. An independent offline audit verified both native hulls, crews, machine blocks, inventories, unique fares, and a settled world without extra VS ships.

hostedWideDefaultPreview.scope: Default dedicated-server configuration, two Chinese survival clients and two prepared 300 × 19 × 8-block ships, both confirmed on the same tick. Actual template plots matched both forecasts and all cargo, machines, fares, passengers and ship records passed independent offline audit. Native assembly still consumed one long tick per ship.
